Formulation:
Patient is a middle-aged male presenting with six weeks of persistent fatigue and diffuse musculoskeletal aching following recent travel to the USA. The onset was insidious, beginning approximately two weeks post-return from an active holiday, with a transient rash on the calf consistent with erythema migrans and mild systemic symptoms (sore throat, low-grade fever) at that time. Relevant past medical history includes asthma and hay fever. Psychologically, he reports good mood and mental resilience despite physical symptoms. Social support appears stable with wife at home. The principal concern is a likely infectious etiology (notably Lyme disease, given his travel history and rash), with differential considerations including post-infectious viral syndrome and early autoimmune disease. The physical symptoms are impacting occupational function and exercise levels. Protective psychosocial factors may support coping while investigations proceed.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Fatigue and generalized aching possibly due to Lyme disease or post-infectious syndrome
- Patient Goal(s): To improve energy levels and reduce musculoskeletal pain, maintain usual functional capacity at work
- Clinical Goal(s): To confirm or exclude Lyme disease and other infectious or inflammatory causes; address physical symptoms and support mental wellbeing during investigation period
- Actions (Patient): Undergo recommended blood tests including Lyme disease screening; monitor symptoms; engage in follow-up consultation post-testing
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Arrange comprehensive blood tests (including infection markers, Lyme serology, inflammatory markers); provide education regarding potential diagnosis and management; schedule telephone follow-up approximately one week post-test; assess mental health status regularly

Secondary Problem: Potential early autoimmune disease or post-infectious fatigue syndrome
- Patient Goal(s): Understand cause of symptoms; prevent symptom progression
- Clinical Goal(s): Monitor for development of joint swelling, stiffness, or other systemic symptoms; consider rheumatology referral if autoimmune disease suspected
- Actions (Patient): Report new or worsening symptoms promptly
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Review blood test results; consider further investigations or specialist referral based on clinical evolution

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Explanation of Lyme disease and possible infectious causes; rationale for blood testing; symptoms to monitor including rash, joint swelling, neurological symptoms
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: New rash development, joint swelling, fever, neurological symptoms, worsening fatigue or mood changes
- Coping Strategies: Maintaining regular communication with healthcare provider; pacing activities; using social support from spouse

Consent, Coordination & Review:
- Patient Consent to Plan: Yes
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: Not recorded
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not applicable
- Review Date: Approximately one week after blood tests completion

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Lyme disease: High likelihood due to rash consistent with erythema migrans, musculoskeletal symptoms, and travel history to endemic area; directly supported and investigated per transcript and DDx reasoning
- Post-infectious viral syndrome: Medium likelihood considering mild sore throat, low-grade fever, and persistent fatigue without ongoing infection signs; supported by DDx and consistent with transcript
- Early autoimmune disease (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis or lupus): Medium likelihood due to generalized aching and transient rash; no joint swelling or other systemic symptoms yet; to be monitored

Quality checks
● Missing but clinically expected elements: Sleep assessment, detailed mental status description, emergency contact
● Internal conflicts between transcript and DDx: None noted; DDx supports clinical impressions from transcript
● Transcript quality notes: Clear audio and complete dialogue; no significant communication barriers noted
